challenges.claim: The row quotes לְדַרְי֖וֹשׁ הַדָּבָֽר byte-exact and glosses it 'to investigate the matter'. The quoted form cannot bear that sense, and the book itself supplies the control. The preposition-plus-infinitive of the verb meaning to seek or investigate is attested in this book at Ezra.7.10 as לִדְר֛וֹשׁ — hireq under the prefixed preposition, shewa under the dalet, and no yod (skeleton sweep: 1 book-wide for that spelling). The 10:16 form is pointed differently at every position — shewa, then patah, then shewa — and carries a yod before the waw; its skeleton is the one that stands at Ezra.5.5 and Ezra.5.7 (skeleton sweep: 3 book-wide, those two plus Ezra.10.16), where it is the preposition prefixed to the royal name. No qere licenses a different reading here either: in this chapter OSHB carries ketiv-qere as adjacent unpointed-plus-pointed twins (as at 10:2 and 10:12), and this word has no twin. The gloss therefore imports a conjectural emendation of a byte-quoted form without disclosure — precisely the class of error that the rule requiring original-language claims to be demonstrated rather than asserted exists to catch. The span is not affected; the reported sense of the quoted evidence is.

challenges.claim: The row makes 10:19 'a summary covering the whole priestly party'. Hebrew syntax does not deliver that. וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ יָדָ֖ם is a wayyiqtol 3mp with no expressed subject, and a wayyiqtol recovers its subject from the clause it continues — here the men listed in 10:18b after the athnach (מִבְּנֵ֨י יֵשׁ֤וּעַ and those named with him). Its predication does not reach forward across 10:20-22, which are verbless noun phrases headed by וּמִבְּנֵ֣י (10:20), וּמִבְּנֵ֖י (10:21) and וּמִבְּנֵ֖י (10:22) and supply no verb for a pledge to distribute into. The clause that does govern them is the class-level finding clause of 10:18, וַיִּמָּצֵא֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֹשִׁ֖יבוּ נָשִׁ֣ים נָכְרִיּ֑וֹת, under which each partitive-plus-name entry hangs, and the accent break inside 10:18 marks precisely that hierarchy. This is not a quarrel over paraphrase: the row defeats its strongest rival (a split at 10:19|10:20) with the pledge-scope reading, so the rebuttal leans on a scope the grammar withholds. The sound ground is already written into the row's own rejected_alternative sentence — the class-header structure treating the priesthood as one office-class.

primary_reviews.rationale: The office-class change at 10:23 is real, the move back to laity at 10:25 is real, and the row reads the compression correctly: three groups across two verses, singers and gatekeepers sharing 10:24. Masoretic accentuation supports the internal division the row describes — athnach sits on אֶלְיָשִׁ֑יב, cutting 10:24 between the singers' entry and the gatekeepers' (tier-2, corroborating rather than driving). Probing the row's implicit hierarchy claim, I found it better founded than its prose states: these three headers share one shape, partitive preposition plus article plus absolute plural, whereas the priestly header at 10:18 inserts a bound form (מִבְּנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים) and the lay header at 10:25 takes a proper noun with the nun of the preposition assimilated (וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל, dagesh in the yod). So the block does stand between two differently shaped headers, which is a stronger warrant than the row gives itself. My objection is to the grammatical label placed on that evidence.

challenges.claim: The row has singers and gatekeepers 'each introduced by its own construct', quoting וּמִן הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים and וּמִן הַשֹּׁ֣עֲרִ֔ים. Neither phrase is a construct chain. הַלְוִיִּ֑ם at 10:23 and the two nouns inside 10:24 are determined absolute plurals governed by a partitive preposition; no nomen regens in the bound state occurs in any of the three. The bound form in this register is the plural construct of ben, as in מִבְּנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים at 10:18 and in the clan headers וּמִבְּנֵ֣י at 10:20-22. Applying one term to both header types erases the morphological contrast that is in fact this row's best warrant for treating 10:23-24 as parallel minor entries rather than major divisions: the contrast with 10:18 (preposition + bound form + determined noun) and with 10:25 (preposition + proper noun).
challenges.suggested_action: Relabel the 10:23-24 headers as partitive min plus determined absolute office-nouns, reserve 'construct' for the ben-headed clan entries, and make the shape contrast with 10:18 and 10:25 the stated ground for the block's internal parallelism.

primary_reviews.rationale: A tight two-verse row bounded by two real class-header shifts: 10:23 opens on the Levites away from the priestly clans just closed, and 10:25 pivots to 'and from Israel' -- laity, a functionally distinct group from the cultic office-classes. Grouping Levites, singers, and gatekeepers into one row rather than three matches the same three-office cluster's own earlier precedent in Ezra 2 (2:40-42), where the golah register treats these minor cultic classes as parallel entries under one heading rather than as major divisions. The rejected alternative (giving singers and gatekeepers their own rows) is a real option textually -- each does carry its own construct header -- but the strategy's own block map and the in-book parallel both back the row's reading of these as minor, not major, class breaks.

The repair swaps v0's unspecified appeal to "class-header grammar" for a morphological rule and then leans the whole ranking argument on it: the partitive-preposition-plus-determined-absolute shape at 10:23-24 is said to be "distinct from the construct clan headers governing the priestly and laity entries at 10:18 and 10:25, which marks these three as parallel minor entries rather than major divisions." The row's own closing quotation refutes the rule. The laity's class-tier header at 10:25 is וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל, partitive mem plus an absolute proper noun -- no construct anywhere in it -- and it is the same shape as וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם at 10:23; the construct form at 10:25 (מִבְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֡שׁ) sits one tier further down, at clan level. Accentuation confirms the tiering: athnach falls on the first word of 10:25, isolating the class header (byte-checked against oshb:Ezra.10.25). So on the row's own discriminator the laity would rank as a minor entry, which the same sentence-chain denies ("a functionally distinct social class"). v1 also rewrote strongest_rejected_alternative from "class-header grammar" to "partitive-header shape," so both content fields now rest on the refuted rule, where v0's vaguer formulation carried no such exposure. primary_reviews.rationale: Both edges survive scrutiny, and the accents make the front edge plainer than the prose does: at 10:25 athnach falls on the opening word וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל, isolating the class name from the clan header מִבְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֡שׁ standing under it — the same two-tier arrangement athnach draws inside 10:18 (tier-2 corroboration). At the rear, 10:43 is an ordinary clan header with names while 10:44 changes clause type, so the close is right. The row's internal descriptions also check out against the pointed text: the lay Harim entry does run through 10:31-32 with no fresh header, the second Bani group does run 10:34-42 the same way, and both stay inside one office-class, so the granularity call is sound. Three problems remain — the row states its own class/clan rule in terms that collapse the two tiers, it asserts a formal sameness across the span that the header morphology contradicts, and it argues verses in prose that its refs array does not carry.

challenges.claim: 'The same repeated construct that headed the priestly and Levitical clans' fails on both halves. (a) The Levitical entries carry no construct form whatever: 10:23-24 head with a partitive preposition plus a determined absolute (וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם, and the two headers inside 10:24), and a skeleton sweep of the clan-header spelling the row has in view (וּמִבְּנֵ֣י) returns 18 verses book-wide with neither 10:23 nor 10:24 among them. (b) The phrase quoted spans two tiers of the register at once: וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל is the class header, set off by athnach, while מִבְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֡שׁ is the clan entry beneath it — the arrangement 10:18 also shows, where athnach separates the class clause from מִבְּנֵ֨י יֵשׁ֤וּעַ. The conflation matters because the row's granularity rule is to divide at class change and not at clan change; calling class header and clan header one construct dissolves the very distinction that rule needs.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate 10:25 as class header plus its opening clan entry, cite the 10:23-24 headers by their own shape instead of assimilating them to the ben-headed clans, and derive the span from the class tier: the office-class holds from 10:25 through 10:43 and changes at the colophon.

challenges.claim: The clan headers inside the span are not formally uniform, and the rationale asserts continuity 'running through 10:43' without registering the shifts. Skeleton sweep of וּמִבְּנֵ֖י as a consonantal string: 18 verses book-wide, whose chapter-10 hits are 10:20-22 and 10:26-30, with no hit after 10:30. At 10:31 the header drops the preposition: וּבְנֵ֖י חָרִ֑ם. From 10:33 the conjunction goes as well: מִבְּנֵ֖י חָשֻׁ֑ם, then מִבְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔י at 10:34, then the closing header מִבְּנֵ֖י נְב֑וֹ at 10:43. (Word-final skeleton sweep of the 10:31 spelling: 5 verses book-wide, chapter-10 hits 10:31 and 10:38, of which 10:38 is the personal name Bani rather than a header; the same string without a word boundary returns 13 verses, so the toolkit's caution on substring sweeps applies.) My own position is that none of these shifts co-occurs with a class change, a participant change or any other tier-1 signal, so none warrants a seam and the span stands as drawn — but the row should argue that rather than assert a sameness the morphology contradicts.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the claim of one repeated construct running through 10:43 with a statement that the header shape varies at 10:31 and again from 10:33 while the office-class holds constant, so the variation carries no seam weight.

challenges.claim: Mirroring gap. The rationale argues 10:31-32 and 10:34-42 in prose, yet boundary_evidence_refs carries 10:24, 10:25, 10:43 and 10:44 and nothing else, leaving eleven argued verses unmirrored. The Tier-0 refs-mirror check reports GREEN on this cluster because it matches ref tokens shaped Ezra.C.V while this rationale writes bare chapter:verse ranges, so the gap is invisible to the machine rather than absent. I verified this by running the checker over the cluster file: 4 rows checked, 0 flags.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:Ezra.10.31, oshb:Ezra.10.32 and oshb:Ezra.10.34 through oshb:Ezra.10.42 to boundary_evidence_refs (bare refs, no annotation).

primary_reviews.rationale: The span itself is right and the granularity argument is one of the stronger pieces of reasoning in the cluster: it correctly declines to split at every lay clan-header (Parosh, Elam, Zattu, Bebai, Bani, Pahath-moab, a second Harim, Hashum, a second Bani, Nebo) because none of those headers cross an office-class line the way 10:23's cultic offices do relative to 10:18's priests. I independently verified the two interior facts the row leans on: a lay clan named Harim heads 10:31 and its five names run into 10:32 without the header repeating, and a second Bani-headed group opens 10:34 and runs unbroken with no repeated header all the way to 10:42 (nine verses, one heading). Both are accurate. But the row cites this interior verse-level evidence -- 10:23 (by cross-reference), 10:31-32, and 10:34-42 -- without mirroring any of those three citations into boundary_evidence_refs, which lists only the span edges (10:24, 10:25, 10:43, 10:44). See the challenge below.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale argues specific interior verse content -- 'the way 10:23-24's cultic offices do' (contrast), Harim's second occurrence spanning 10:31-32 (header not repeated), and a second Bani group spanning 10:34-42 (header not repeated for nine verses) -- as evidence for the row's granularity conclusion, but none of 10:23, 10:31, 10:32, or 10:34 through 10:42 appear in boundary_evidence_refs, which holds only oshb:Ezra.10.24, 10.25, 10.43, 10.44. check_refs_mirror.py returns GREEN on this row only because its verse-citation regex matches the 'Ezra.C.V' dot form and this row cites in 'C:V' colon form throughout, so the tool cannot see the gap -- confirmed by running the checker directly against cluster_08.json and cross-checking its regex against the row's actual citation style.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:Ezra.10.23, oshb:Ezra.10.31, oshb:Ezra.10.32, and oshb:Ezra.10.34 through oshb:Ezra.10.42 (or equivalent range tokens) to boundary_evidence_refs so the interior claims this row's argument depends on are traceable the same way its edges are.

primary_reviews.rationale: The newly added clan-header-progression sentence mis-describes the very forms it quotes. It narrates a cumulative stripping -- the conjunction-plus-partitive-plus-construct spelling "repeats through 10:30, then drops the partitive at 10:31, וּבְנֵ֖י חָרִ֑ם ..., and drops the conjunction too from 10:33 on, מִבְּנֵ֖י חָשֻׁ֑ם" -- but the 10:33 form restores the partitive mem that 10:31 had dropped while dropping the conjunction; "too" implies a further-stripped shape carrying neither element, which is not what stands there. Byte-checked slices: 10:31 וּבְנֵ֖י חָרִ֑ם, 10:33 מִבְּנֵ֖י חָשֻׁ֑ם, 10:34 מִבְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔י, 10:43 מִבְּנֵ֖י נְב֑וֹ. The row's own glosses read the morphology correctly ('and sons of' at 10:31 against 'of the sons of' from 10:33), so the prose and the glosses disagree with each other inside one clause. (+1 further finding(s); see challenges)

The row's conclusion -- that the alternation tracks no class change and carries no seam weight -- survives the correction untouched.

challenges.claim: The repair recruits an accentual corroboration that cannot discriminate the tier it is offered for: "the class header וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ..., athnach-marked like the class-level finding clause at 10:18." Athnach closes the header phrase in ordinary clan-header verses throughout this same register -- 10:21 חָרִ֑ם, 10:22 פַּשְׁח֑וּר, 10:26 עֵילָ֑ם, 10:27 זַתּ֑וּא, 10:28 בֵּבָ֑י, 10:29 בָּנִ֑י, 10:31 חָרִ֑ם, 10:33 חָשֻׁ֑ם, 10:43 נְב֑וֹ: nine clan headers, counted over oshb Ezra.10.16-10.44, i.e. over precisely the headers this row declares to carry "no seam weight of its own." As written the accent reads as evidence for the class/clan distinction while being neutral between the two, which leaves the class tier resting on the class nouns alone.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the athnach comparison, or keep it with the count disclosed and its force stated plainly -- a tier-2 clause-level accent, ubiquitous in this register's entry verses, corroborating the verse-internal division at 10:25 but saying nothing about class rank.

primary_reviews.rationale: The colophon identification is correct, and the Hebrew supports it more firmly than the row claims. כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה is a book-wide singleton: skeleton sweep of that pair returns 1 verse of 280. Finite predication returns at 10:44 after twenty-four verses of headers and names, 10:20 through 10:43, that carry no finite verb — the graphic ketiv ויעשו at 10:37 is read as the personal name וְיַעֲשָֽׂי, so it is no exception. The verb also changes: the chapter states the offence with the hiphil of yashab (וַנֹּ֛שֶׁב at 10:2, וַתֹּשִׁ֖יבוּ at 10:10, הַהֹשִׁ֞יב at 10:14, הַהֹשִׁ֖יבוּ at 10:17, הֹשִׁ֖יבוּ at 10:18), whereas the qere at 10:44 is נָשְׂא֖וּ, the verb of the crisis report at 9:2, כִּֽי נָשְׂא֣וּ מִבְּנֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם — an in-book lexical return that fits the row's claim that this verse closes the wider intermarriage unit and not merely the register. (Skeleton sweep of that root spelling: 6 verses book-wide; the 9:15 hit is נִשְׁאַ֥רְנוּ, a different root caught as a substring, per the toolkit caution.) The ketiv/qere is disclosed as the discipline requires, which is the principal original-language obligation at this verse, and the English parenthesis is marked as a construal rather than passed off as text — though for the record WEB reads 'Some of them had wives by whom they had children.', which is not the wording the row prints. Two small repairs remain.

challenges.claim: 'Its verb spans a ketiv/qere pair' merges two readings that differ in clause type. The consonantal ketiv נשאי ends in yod and reads naturally as a bound plural participle in apposition to כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה ('takers of' foreign wives), which leaves 10:44a verbless; the qere נָשְׂא֖וּ is a 3cp perfect and yields a finite predicate. The strongest colophon argument available here — that 10:44 restores finite predication after the verbless entry-verses of 10:20-43 — holds on the qere and softens on the ketiv, so the reading the warrant uses should be named rather than folded into one 'verb'.
challenges.suggested_action: Distinguish ketiv (participial, nominal apposition) from qere (finite perfect), keep both forms disclosed as they already are, and state that the colophon warrant follows the qere.

challenges.claim: The closing clause — 'As the final verse of the book, it closes the register and the larger intermarriage-crisis unit without further narrative resumption' — argues closure from the absence of anything following, at the one position in the book where nothing could follow. Such an argument cannot fail and therefore carries no weight, and campaign practice treats absence as non-evidence for a seam. The positive signals do the work without it: the summative opener כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה, the return of finite predication after 10:20-43, and the switch from the chapter's hiphil idiom to the verb of 9:2.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the no-resumption clause and rest the close on the summative opener, the restored finite predication, and the lexical return to 9:2's verb; mirror oshb:Ezra.9.2 into the refs if that lexical point is adopted.

primary_reviews.rationale: The colophon reading is defensible on the text: 'all these' does summarize the whole preceding register rather than adding one more clan-name entry, and the ketiv/qere pair on the verb is disclosed rather than silently resolved, and the closing English gloss is honestly attributed as 'per WEB's construal' rather than presented as a verbatim WEB quote (WEB's clean text actually reads 'Some of them had wives by whom they had children' -- close in sense, not identical wording, and the row does not claim identity). What I cannot square is the confidence label. The book strategy's own §7 names '10:44 closing-formula attachment' as one of its ~10 expected low-confidence regions and says explicitly not to default to uniform high. This row's strongest_rejected_alternative is exactly that contested attachment question -- fold 10:44 into 10:25-43 as a closing line, versus give it its own colophon row -- and the row resolves it at 'high' with no acknowledgment that the strategy flagged this precise seam as a site of expected honest dissent.

challenges.claim: Strategy §7 lists '10:44 closing-formula attachment' among the expected low-confidence regions and states 'Honest mix expected per campaign precedent -- do NOT default uniform high.' This row's own strongest_rejected_alternative is precisely that attachment question (colophon-as-own-row versus fold into 10:25-43), yet confidence is set to high with no warrant given for departing from the strategy's flagged uncertainty on this exact seam.
challenges.suggested_action: Lower confidence to medium, or if high is retained, add explicit warrant for why this instance overrides the strategy's flagged low-confidence expectation -- for example, disclosing the tier-3 single-witness PE mark WLC places after 10:44 (pmarks_Ezra.json) as weak corroboration for a major break at the book's close, while being clear it is corroboration only and not a driver.

primary_reviews.rationale: v1 newly tags the colophon's opening כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה as "a book-wide singleton" and cites no count beside it. The fact is right -- a skeleton sweep of that phrase returns 1 hit book-wide (Ezra.10.44), against 93 for the bare demonstrative skeleton -- but the standing rule wants the number adjacent to the claim, and this one is invisible to the machinery: check_universals.py run over the v1 rows returns claims_seen 0, status GREEN, because "singleton" is outside its universal lexicon and the words "book-wide" themselves satisfy its sweep-citation pattern. The tag is not ornamental either; uniqueness of the opening formula is part of what separates the colophon from the entry verses above it. (+2 further finding(s); see challenges)

challenges.claim: The new qere argument over-reaches: the qere נָשְׂא֖וּ is said to be "a finite 3cp perfect that restores finite predication after the register's run of verbless entry-verses (10:20-43) -- the colophon's return to a finite verb follows the qere specifically." The ketiv/qere pair covers only נשאי / נָשְׂא֖וּ. The verse's other finite verb, וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ in the qualifying note this row quotes two clauses later, is a wayyiqtol on either reading, so 10:44 returns to finite predication whichever way the pair is taken. Only the finiteness of the summative main clause turns on the qere, not the colophon's.
challenges.suggested_action: Scope the claim to the summative כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה clause and drop "specifically," noting that וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ supplies finite predication in the verse independently of the ketiv/qere choice.

challenges.claim: The repair's new 9:2 comparandum is credited to the wrong voice and the wrong clause: "the predicate echoes the same inflected form Ezra's own report opens with at 9:2, נָשְׂא֣וּ מִבְּנֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם." The slice is byte-accurate, but 9:2 lies inside speech reported TO Ezra -- 9:1 נִגְּשׁ֨וּ אֵלַ֤י הַשָּׂרִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר makes the officials the speakers of what follows -- and that report opens at 9:1 with לֹֽא נִבְדְּל֞וּ, the verb standing at 9:2 only in the subsequent causal clause. The framing therefore overstates both the speaker and the position of the form the inclusio is built on.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-attribute to the officials' report to Ezra at 9:1-2 and drop "opens with," or keep the echo as an inclusio on the crisis unit's naming verb without claiming initial position for it. The inclusio itself is unaffected.
